To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stress level of the Arts and Science College Teachers is moderate and the most important factors that contribute to stress among the teachers are workload, work environment, and work life balance. And
the stress is a major problem in the work place and the teachers are not able to cope up with the stress.
The teachers are facing the workplace stress in their work place, The stress is more for the female teachers than the male teachers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stress and its effects among Arts and science college teachers, the factors which contribute to stress, and the coping strategies that are used to manage the stress.
the relationship between the work environment and stress, and the impact of stress on the performance and well-being of employees.
the relationship between workplace stressors and coping strategies among Arts and Science College teachers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, workplace stress is the most common problem in today’s work environment.
, the stressors that are most likely to be experienced in the workplace are the ones that are most likely not to be controlled by the employee.
, the study revealed that, the workplace stress and the coping strategies among Arts and Science College Teachers in Kanyakumuri District is high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of our study show that the majority of the teachers have moderate level of stress.
stress is a common problem in today's workplace, but it can be managed effectively.
stress management is a very complex process, and that it is important to recognize that the causes of stress and the strategies to manage it are different for each individual.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one best way to manage stress.
the most common causes of stress are work overload, lack of control, role ambiguity and conflict, and interpersonal relationships at work.
the stressors and the stress responses of the employees of the organizations in India are similar to that of the developed world and hence the coping mechanisms need to be similar.
